transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I... I came in because I just can't shake this feeling lately. It's at work—I'm a teacher, secondary school, mostly history and a little geography when they need me to fill in. But anyway, it's the staff emails and the morning announcements. I just know they're actually coded messages about me. My colleagues, they try to be gentle about it, you know, they show me the emails and say, "Look, this went to the whole staff list," but... it doesn't change what I know is there. It's like that time I found a stray cat near the cafeteria, just wandering around by the bins. It had this little bell on its collar that kept ringing, and I spent half my lunch break trying to catch it before the kids got out. The principal was so annoyed, but I couldn't just leave it there. Anyway, the emails... they just feel so pointed, even if everyone else's name is on the "To" line.
About how long have you been feeling that these emails and announcements are directed at you?

Well, let me think... it's been about four months now. Right around the time we had the autumn half-term. I remember because the weather turned so quickly this year, didn't it? One week we were all still in our light jackets, and the next, the heating completely broke down in the humanities block. It was absolutely freezing. I had to bring in this little portable space heater from home, the one I usually keep in the conservatory. But the site manager, Dave—he’s a lovely man, but very strict on health and safety—he came right into my classroom and told me I couldn't use it. He actually confiscated it and put it in his office, which was a bit ridiculous because his office is always boiling anyway. 

But, oh, anyway, yes... about four months. That's how long the worries about the coded messages have been going on. And... well, it's been about that long for the voice, too. The one I sometimes answer. It all sort of started right around the time Dave took my heater, actually. I just remember standing there feeling so terribly cold while I was trying to read the morning bulletin...
Over these past four months, how has your mood generally been?

My mood? Well, I haven't really noticed a change in my mood, to be honest. I suppose I've just felt... fine? Normal, really. Just terribly busy. I mean, as normal as you can feel when you're trying to get Year 9s to actually care about the Industrial Revolution. 

We just started the unit on the textile industry last week, and I actually bought some raw cotton off the internet to pass around the class. I thought it would be a nice tactile experience for them, you know? Bring history to life a bit. But half of them just pulled it apart and started throwing it at each other when my back was turned. One boy, Thomas—he's a bright lad but absolutely no impulse control—he managed to flick a clump of it right up onto the projector lens. It started smoking after a few minutes, and the smell was absolutely terrible, like burnt hair. We had to open all the windows, which completely defeated the whole purpose of getting the heating fixed in the first place. The IT technician, poor Gareth, had to come in with a stepladder right in the middle of my lesson to scrape it off. 

So, yes, it's just been the usual sort of chaos, really. I haven't had much time to sit and think about how I'm feeling. What were you asking me again? Something about the term?
